name: Carousel
statusNote: Post-M2 component; no comp.carousel tokens exist yet (verified: a key scan for "carousel" in tokens/m3e.resolved.json returns empty).
summary: A horizontal (or vertical) scroller that shows a mix of large, medium, and small items so several pieces of visual content are browsable at once, with items masking/expanding as they scroll toward the edge. Choose it over a standard scroll view when items should snap and change size near the edges.

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: The carousel's scroll/settle state object; exposes the settled page index and a jump-without-animation operation.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: Per-item content, indexed by item position; drawn full-size and clipped to the item's current mask rect as it scrolls.

inputs.name: strategy
inputs.description: Which keyline algorithm arranges items: multi-browse solves large/medium/small counts jointly; uncontained is one uniform item width with a deliberately cut-off last item and no snap; hero variants show one or more large items with small peek item(s); full-screen is the degenerate case with no room for small items.

inputs.name: preferredItemWidth
inputs.description: Multi-browse/uncontained/hero: the width in dp the carousel aims for on its large (or uniform, for uncontained) item; hero's default targets the whole viewport.

inputs.name: itemSpacing
inputs.description: The space between items, in dp.

inputs.name: contentPadding
inputs.description: Padding around the whole content, before the first item and after the last, in dp.

inputs.name: minSmallItemWidth
inputs.description: The minimum allowable width of small items, in dp.

inputs.name: maxSmallItemWidth
inputs.description: The maximum allowable width of small items, in dp.

inputs.name: userScrollEnabled
inputs.description: Whether scrolling via user gestures or accessibility actions is allowed.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The scrollable viewport; clips items to it.

anatomy.name: Large item
anatomy.description: The fully visible, focal item size.

anatomy.name: Medium item
anatomy.description: Partially cut off, present only in multi-browse.

anatomy.name: Small item
anatomy.description: The most-cut-off item, present in multi-browse and hero.

anatomy.name: Item content
anatomy.description: Each item's own content (image, text), drawn full-size and clipped to the item's current mask rect as it scrolls.

variants.description: Quick browsing of many similar items (thumbnails, album art); one or more large + medium + small items, sizes solved jointly per available width.
One item size throughout, last item deliberately cut off at the edge; uniform item width plus one cut-off item.
One or more large items with a small peek at the edge; one or more large + one small.
A centered large item flanked by two small items; requires at least 3 items to center.
Degenerate hero/multi-browse with no room for small items; one large item filling the viewport.

layout.text: No dedicated tokens exist for item sizes; CarouselDefaults supplies the only defaults: min small item size, max small item size, item spacing, content padding, and an internal anchor size used for the sliver of a small/edge item that stays visible.

Multi-browse solves item sizes by targeting a small item at 1/3 of the large item's size, clamped to [minSmallItemSize, maxSmallItemSize], and a medium size at the midpoint of large and small, then finds the lowest-cost integer arrangement of large/medium/small counts that fills the available width.
Hero targets the same 1/3-of-large small size, requires 2 small items to center (else 1, start-aligned), and forces start-alignment when fewer than 3 items exist even if centering was requested.

Hero collapses to full-screen (0 small items) when available space is below smallCount * minSmallItemSize + minSmallItemSize * 1.25 — i.e. there isn't room for the required small items plus a large item at least 25% bigger than them.

Uncontained sizes its cut-off (medium) sliver via remainingSpace * 1.5, clamped so it never exceeds 85% of the large item size — past that threshold the sliver is judged "too similar" to a full item and is shrunk back to a 20%-cut-off size instead.

Items snap to keyline positions; a mask clip/border on each item clips content to the intersection of the item's own bounds and its current mask rect, which is what produces the expand/collapse look as an item crosses from small to medium to large.

states.label: settle
states.text: Scrolling and snapping are pager-based, one focal page per settle; the state exposes the settled page index and a jump-without-animation operation. Programmatic scrolls further than 3 pages away animate via a synthetic short hop instead of scrolling every intermediate page.

states.label: fling-snap
states.text: Fling/snap does not use a named sys.motion.spring — it uses a raw spring(stiffness = StiffnessMediumLow) as the snap-approach spec for both the single-advance (multi-browse/hero default) and free-fling behaviors. A high-velocity fling first decays via a spline-based decay curve, then hands off to that spring for the final snap. Uncontained carousels use a no-snap fling behavior instead — velocity-based fling with no post-fling snap at all.

behaviour.text: No dedicated press/hover/focus/selected item states are defined by Carousel itself; those are the responsibility of whatever content each item composes (e.g. a Card).
An optional parallax effect can translate/clip item content as it enters and exits the viewport, independent of the snap/fling behavior.

Multi-browse, hero, and uncontained are three separate keyline algorithms, not one algorithm with a mode flag — a generic renderer should implement them as distinct strategies matching multiBrowseKeylineList, heroKeylineList, and uncontainedKeylineList.

keyboard: Scrolling to the next/previous item must be operable without a drag gesture (e.g. next/previous actions), since carousels are drag-first by design.
semantics: The container behaves as a scrollable list/group; each item is a member of that group and should expose its own accessible name from its content.
Item content controls (e.g. a play button on a media item) must still meet the 48dp minimum even when the item itself is masked down to a small (40-56dp) sliver.
Screen reader should announce position within the carousel (e.g. "item 3 of 8") since visually only a few items are ever on screen at once.

notes.text: There is no comp.carousel token group to theme against; a design system built on this kit must either add one or theme individual items using existing card/list tokens for their content, leaving only the sizing/snap behavior above as carousel-specific.

minSmallItemSize/maxSmallItemSize/anchorSize/mediumLargeItemDiffThreshold are Compose-internal constants, not tokens — treat them as reasonable starting defaults to expose as configuration, not values to hard-code permanently.
